strategy.title: October acquisition plan
strategy.summary: Grow rental customers while keeping acquisition costs within a declared ceiling.
strategy.body:
Audience: event planners and venue owners seeking outdoor rental space.

Priorities: test the rental offer across paid search and partnerships; improve consultation handoffs; measure organic landing-page acquisition.

Guardrails: reconcile all marketing expenses before changing budgets. Review experiments against validated SQL and customer outcomes.

Review: assess targets weekly, prepare recommendations automatically in a connected system, and keep material execution subject to owner approval.

Illustrative strategy only; these goals have not been approved for the live business.

hypotheses.title: Test an availability-led rental funnel
hypotheses.audience: Event planners in the declared service area
hypotheses.handoff: Validated inquiry → sales acceptance → booked consultation → attended → first Won contract
hypotheses.criterion: Primary: 5 validated SQL in the 14-day pilot. Review booked consultations and customers before expansion; stop and investigate if tracking is incomplete.
hypotheses.budget: Up to $500 ad spend · 14 full days · owner review before launch
hypotheses.measurement: New funnel pilot. Compare with the same declared audience and period basis for context; multiple changed dimensions do not isolate a causal effect. Establish funnel IDs, attribution and deduplication before collection.
hypotheses.dependencies: Proposed funnel only. Confirm CRM qualification, booking linkage, attribution and allocated costs. Confirm launch permissions in the execution tool.
hypotheses.hypothesis: An availability-led offer for high-intent rental searches may produce more validated SQL within the declared pilot budget.

evidence.source: Sample · scoped CRM, booking and expense reports
evidence.summary: October: 3 new customers against a monthly target of 30. The venue pilot recorded 5 validated SQL and 1 new customer; those results belong to its own funnel.
evidence.limit: Seven days of monthly progress are incomplete. Cross-channel differences do not establish why one funnel performs better.

hypotheses.next: Prepare a separate rental-search pilot with a named offer and landing page.

hypotheses.title: Test the consultation handoff
hypotheses.audience: Event planners in the declared service area
hypotheses.handoff: Validated inquiry → sales acceptance → booked consultation → attended → first Won contract
hypotheses.criterion: Primary: booking rate of at least 60% in the eligible contact cohort. Keep attendance at or above the predeclared comparable baseline; verify assignment and sample size before any causal conclusion.
hypotheses.budget: Up to $150 preparation cost · observe 14 days and complete the booking window
hypotheses.measurement: Controlled message test proposal. Change one invitation, define eligible contacts, randomize stable contact assignment, freeze the comparison window and predeclare sample size with the analyst. No test is launched here.
hypotheses.dependencies: Proposed funnel only. Confirm CRM qualification, booking linkage, attribution and allocated costs. Confirm launch permissions in the execution tool.
hypotheses.hypothesis: A clearer scheduling invitation after fit confirmation may raise the same-cohort booking rate without increasing no-shows.

evidence.source: Sample · scoped CRM, booking and expense reports
evidence.summary: Booking rate is 57.1% against a minimum target of 60%: a gap of 2.9 percentage points.
evidence.limit: The current observation is a scoped rate, not proof that the invitation caused the gap. Confirm booking and attendance coverage.

hypotheses.next: Inspect the handoff, then prepare a controlled invitation test.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A venue planning guide matched to organic search intent may attract more qualified inquiries in the declared landing-page cohort.

evidence.limit: Organic acquisition is a distinct attributed cohort. Confirm service fit and sales maturity before increasing production.

hypotheses.next: Prepare an organic guide pilot with a named landing page and validated CRM qualification.

experiments.title: Venue search pilot
experiments.criterion: Pilot criterion: at least 5 validated SQL, complete booking linkage and up to $400 attributed marketing costs.
experiments.measurement: Declared seven-day pilot, complete synthetic records. No randomized control. Costs include $280 ads and $80 allocated preparation. This is an operational observation, not an A/B winner.
experiments.recommendation: The declared SQL and cost criteria were met in this sample. Review customer maturity and capacity before proposing a larger pilot; one acquired customer is weak scaling evidence.

experiments.title: Venue partnership outreach pilot
experiments.criterion: Primary: 4 validated SQL over 14 days. Complete the response and booking window before judging.
experiments.measurement: Declared contact cohort. No causal comparison is supplied. Allocated preparation costs are not reconciled yet.

learnings.title: Venue intent produced qualified demand in the pilot
learnings.finding: 12 unique leads included 7 MQL and 5 SQL. In the same lead cohort, 6 booked consultations, 4 attended and 1 became a new customer. The SQL criterion and cost ceiling were met. Customer evidence remains sparse.
learnings.context: Sample venue-search-v1 · October 1–7 · selected service area · $360 attributed marketing costs. This is a descriptive pilot outcome; it does not prove uplift or transfer to another audience.
learnings.next: Test rental intent in a separate named funnel; retain the same qualification and booking definitions.
